title: Basic Computer & Internet Literacy
tagline: From the parts of a computer to safe, confident everyday use, with practice in every module
summary: Start from zero. Learn what a computer is and how storage works, manage files and folders, use a browser and search well, write clear emails, keep your accounts and money safe from scams, and fix common problems. Every module has practice labs that check your work and explain what is missing.

modules.title: Meet the computer
modules.summary: Learn what a computer is, what its parts do, how software differs from hardware, and how storage is measured.
modules.outcome: You can name the main parts of a computer or phone, say what each does, and work out how much will fit in a given amount of storage.
modules.intro: A computer is a machine that follows instructions very fast. Phones, laptops, tablets and even smart TVs are all computers. You do not need to know how they are built to use them well, but a small picture of what is inside makes everything else easier to learn, from fixing a slow device to choosing what to buy.

topics.title: Hardware and software
topics.html:
Everything about a computer falls into two groups. Hardware is the physical parts you can touch: the screen, keyboard, battery, the chips inside. Software is the instructions that tell the hardware what to do: the apps, the games, the operating system. Hardware without software does nothing, and software without hardware has nowhere to run.

Definition

Operating system (OS). The main software that manages the hardware and lets you run other programs. Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS are operating systems. It gives you the desktop or home screen, the files and the settings.

Hardware or software?
ItemWhich
Touch screenHardware
AndroidSoftware (an operating system)
A calculator appSoftware (an application)
The batteryHardware
A game you downloadSoftware
Tip

When something goes wrong, ask: is this a hardware problem (a cracked screen, a dead battery) or a software problem (an app that crashes)? Software problems are usually fixed by restarting or updating; hardware problems usually need repair.

Try it yourself: Is WhatsApp hardware or software?

Model answer. Software. It is an application, a program, that runs on the hardware of your phone.

Check what you just learned

1. Which of these is software?
  • The screen
  • Android (correct)
  • The battery
  • The charger

Android is an operating system, which is software.

2. What does the operating system do?
  • Cools the computer
  • Charges the battery
  • Manages the hardware and runs other programs (correct)
  • Makes the screen brighter

It is the main software that everything else relies on.
keyPoints: Hardware is the physical parts; software is the instructions.
The operating system manages the hardware and runs your apps.
Every computer follows input, processing, storage and output.

topics.title: Inside the box: CPU, memory and storage
topics.html:
Three parts explain most of what you will ever hear about speed and space.

The three that matter most
PartWhat it doesEveryday pictureWhat happens when it is full or slow
CPU (processor)Does the calculations and follows instructionsThe brainEverything feels slow when it is overworked
RAM (memory)Holds what is open and in use right now; it empties when power goes offYour deskToo many things open and the device slows down
Storage (SSD or hard disk)Keeps files and apps permanentlyA cupboardYou cannot save new files or install apps
Worked example

Why is my phone slow?

A phone becomes slow and says Storage almost full.

  1. Storage is the cupboard: if it is nearly full the phone struggles to save and swap data.
  2. RAM is the desk: if many apps are open at once the desk is crowded.
  3. First steps: close apps you are not using, delete files you do not need, restart the phone.

Answer. Matching the symptom to the part tells you what to try.

Simple habits that keep a device quick

  • Close apps you are not using.
  • Keep at least a fifth of your storage free.
  • Restart now and then; it clears the desk.
  • Install updates, which often include speed fixes.
Watch out

Do not install 'cleaner' or 'booster' apps from adverts. Many are useless or carry adverts and unwanted software. The built-in storage settings do the same job safely.

Check what you just learned

1. Which part keeps your photos when the phone is switched off?
  • RAM
  • CPU
  • Speaker
  • Storage (correct)

Storage keeps files permanently.

2. Too many open apps mostly crowds:
  • RAM (correct)
  • Storage
  • The battery label
  • The screen

RAM is the working space for what is open now.
keyPoints: CPU is the brain, RAM is the desk, storage is the cupboard.
RAM empties when power goes off; storage keeps files.
Match the symptom to the part to choose a fix.

topics.title: Measuring storage: bytes, MB and GB
topics.html:
The smallest unit is the bit (a 0 or a 1). Eight bits make a byte, roughly one letter. Bigger amounts use prefixes you already know from kilometres and kilograms, but each step is about a thousand times bigger (1,024, to be exact).

Storage units
UnitShortAbout how much
KilobyteKBA short email or a page of plain text
MegabyteMBA photo, or a minute of music
GigabyteGBA film, or hundreds of photos
TerabyteTBA large library of films, or a lot of photos and videos
Formula · Converting units

1 GB = 1,024 MB

To change GB into MB, multiply by 1,024. To change MB into GB, divide by 1,024.

Worked example

How many photos fit?

A phone has 64 GB. The system and apps use 20 GB. One photo takes about 4 MB.

  1. Free space: 64 - 20 = 44 GB.
  2. In megabytes: 44 x 1,024 = 45,056 MB.
  3. Photos: 45,056 / 4 = 11,264 photos.

Answer. Always change both numbers into the same unit before you divide.

How many fit?

Choose the storage and the size of one file.

Adjust Free space (GB), Size of one file (MB) and see How many files fit, Free space in MB change.

Common mistakes

  • Mixing MB and GB without converting.
  • Forgetting that the 64 GB on the box is not all free: the system takes some.
  • Thinking a megabit (Mb, used for internet speed) is the same as a megabyte (MB): a byte is eight bits.

Check what you just learned

1. How many MB are in 1 GB?
  • 10
  • 1,024 (correct)
  • 100
  • 1,000,000

Each step up is 1,024 times.

2. A photo takes 4 MB. About how many fit in 1 GB?
  • 25
  • 4,000
  • 256 (correct)
  • 1

1,024 divided by 4 is 256.

Key terms: flip and sort

Hardware
The physical parts
Software
The instructions: apps and the operating system
Operating system
The main software that manages the device
CPU
The processor that does the work
RAM
Working memory for what is open now
Storage
Where files are kept
keyPoints: Eight bits make a byte; each unit up is about 1,024 times bigger.
Convert to the same unit before you calculate.
A phone's advertised storage is more than what you can use.

modules.title: Files, folders and the desktop
modules.summary: Use windows and the desktop confidently, create and name files, organise them in folders, and use the shortcuts that save the most time.
modules.outcome: You can find any file you have saved, keep your files tidy and use the key shortcuts without thinking.
modules.intro: Most of everyday computing is managing files: saving a document, finding a photo, copying something to a pen drive. People who lose hours looking for files usually have no plan for where things go. This module gives you one, along with the shortcuts every confident user knows.

topics.title: The desktop, windows and apps
topics.html:
The desktop is your main screen: a background, icons for your favourite apps and files, and a bar (the taskbar on Windows, the dock on a Mac) that shows what is open. Every program you open appears in its own window that you can move, resize, minimise and close.

Window controls
ControlDoesTip
Minimise (a dash)Hides the window but keeps the program runningClick its icon in the taskbar to bring it back
Maximise (a square)Makes the window fill the screenDouble-click the title bar does the same
Close (an X)Ends the program or closes the documentSave first!
Drag the title barMoves the windowDrag to the screen edge to snap it half the screen
Tip

Alt+Tab (Windows) or Cmd+Tab (Mac) switches between open programs without touching the mouse.

Common mistakes

  • Closing a document without saving.
  • Opening the same program ten times because the first one is hidden: look in the taskbar.
  • Saving to the Desktop and ending up with a screen full of icons.

Check what you just learned

1. Which control hides a window but keeps the program running?
  • Close
  • Save
  • Maximise
  • Minimise (correct)

Minimise puts it in the taskbar.

2. What does Alt+Tab do?
  • Switches between open programs (correct)
  • Closes a window
  • Saves the file
  • Shuts down

It moves you to the next open program.
keyPoints: The desktop holds icons and a bar of open programs.
Each program runs in a window with minimise, maximise and close.
Alt+Tab or Cmd+Tab switches programs quickly.

topics.title: Files, folders and file types
topics.html:
A file is one thing you saved: a document, a photo, a song. A folder is a container that holds files and other folders. Together they form a tree you can walk down: Documents > School > Science > report.docx.

Common file types
EndingWhat it isOpens with
.docxA Word or Docs documentA word processor
.pdfA page that looks the same on every deviceA PDF reader or a browser
.jpg or .pngA pictureA photo viewer
.mp3A song or audioA music player
.xlsxA spreadsheetA spreadsheet program
.zipA folder squashed into one fileRight-click and Extract

Good names for files

  • Say what it is: Science report, not Document1.
  • Put the date first in year-month-day order: 2026-03-14 Science report.
  • Use v1, v2, v3 for versions; never Final.
  • Avoid symbols such as / ? : * which many systems reject.
Worked example

Find a lost file

You saved a photo yesterday but cannot see it.

  1. Open the search box and type part of the name, or the file type such as .jpg.
  2. Look in Downloads and Pictures first: that is where most files land.
  3. Sort the folder by Date modified, newest first, to see what you touched recently.

Answer. Search and sorting find a file faster than remembering where it is.

Watch out

Be careful with files ending in .exe, .bat or .scr that arrive by email or download. They are programs, and running an unknown one can harm your computer.

Tip

To see the ending of a file name on Windows, open the View menu in File Explorer and tick File name extensions. It helps you spot a file pretending to be a picture that is really a program.

Check what you just learned

1. Which file ending is a picture?
  • .mp3
  • .jpg (correct)
  • .docx
  • .zip

.jpg is a common picture format.

2. Which name is best?
  • Final
  • Document1
  • 2026-03-14 Science report v2 (correct)
  • asdfgh

A date, a topic and a version make it clear.
keyPoints: A folder holds files and other folders in a tree.
The ending of a file name shows its type.
Name files clearly, date first, and sort by date to find recent ones.

topics.title: Copy, move, delete and the shortcuts that save time
topics.html:
You will copy, move and delete files hundreds of times. A few shortcuts turn each of those from three steps into one.

Shortcuts everyone should know
WindowsMacDoes
Ctrl+CCmd+CCopy what is selected
Ctrl+XCmd+XCut (move) what is selected
Ctrl+VCmd+VPaste
Ctrl+ZCmd+ZUndo the last action
Ctrl+SCmd+SSave
Ctrl+ACmd+ASelect everything
Ctrl+FCmd+FFind on the page
Worked example

Move a photo to the right folder

A photo is in Downloads and belongs in Pictures.

  1. Click the photo to select it.
  2. Press Ctrl+X to cut it.
  3. Open the Pictures folder.
  4. Press Ctrl+V to paste. The photo has moved.

Answer. Copy leaves the original; cut moves it.

Deleting safely

  • Delete sends a file to the Recycle Bin (Trash), where you can restore it.
  • Emptying the bin removes the files for good.
  • Before you empty it, look through it once.
  • If something important is gone, stop, check the bin, and then ask for help; do not install 'recovery' programs from adverts.
Try it yourself: You pasted a file into the wrong folder. What is the fastest fix?

Model answer. Press Ctrl+Z to undo, or cut it again and paste it into the right folder.

Tip

Ctrl+Z is the most useful key on the keyboard. If something goes wrong in almost any program, try it before anything else.

Check what you just learned

1. Which shortcut undoes the last action?
  • Ctrl+F
  • Ctrl+S
  • Ctrl+A
  • Ctrl+Z (correct)

Ctrl+Z is undo (Cmd+Z on a Mac).

2. What is the difference between copy and cut?
  • Copy leaves the original; cut moves it (correct)
  • None
  • Cut is faster
  • Copy deletes

Cut removes the original when you paste.

Key terms: flip and sort

Desktop
The main screen with icons and the taskbar
Window
The frame a program runs in
File
One saved item
Folder
A container for files
Extension
The ending of a file name that shows its type
Recycle Bin
Where deleted files wait
keyPoints: Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+X cuts, Ctrl+V pastes, Ctrl+Z undoes.
Cut moves; copy duplicates.
Delete goes to the bin; emptying the bin is permanent.

Empty the Recycle Bin after checking it.

modules.title: The internet and the web
modules.summary: Understand how the internet and the web work, use a browser well, and search in ways that find reliable answers.
modules.outcome: You can read a web address, use browser features, search precisely and judge whether a page can be trusted.
modules.intro: The internet is the giant network of connected computers. The web is just one thing that runs on it: the pages you open in a browser. Email, video calls and apps use the internet too, without being 'the web'. Knowing the difference, and a few browser skills, helps you find what you need and avoid what you do not.

topics.title: How the internet works, in plain words
topics.html:
When you open a page, your device asks another computer, called a server, to send it. That request travels through a chain of cables, wireless links and routers until it reaches the server, and the page comes back the same way, in a fraction of a second.

Words you will hear
WordPlain meaning
ServerA computer that stores pages and sends them when asked
RouterThe box that connects your devices to the internet
Wi-FiA wireless link between your device and the router
Mobile dataInternet over the phone network
BandwidthHow much data can flow at once (more is faster)
CloudOther people's computers that store your files or run your apps
Tip

If a page will not load, check whether other pages work. If none do, the problem is your connection (try restarting the router); if only one site fails, the problem is probably at that site.

Watch out

Free public Wi-Fi in cafes and stations can be watched by others. Do not log into your bank or enter card details on it; use mobile data instead.

Check what you just learned

1. What is a server?
  • A person
  • A computer that stores pages and sends them when asked (correct)
  • A cable
  • A game

Servers store and send websites and other data.

2. Which is safer for online banking?
  • Public Wi-Fi
  • An unknown hotspot
  • Your mobile data or home connection (correct)
  • Any network

Public Wi-Fi can be watched.
keyPoints: The web is one thing that runs on the internet.
A page is requested from a server and sent back.
Avoid sensitive tasks on public Wi-Fi.

topics.title: Using a browser well
topics.html:
A browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) is the app that opens web pages. A web address, or URL, has three parts.

Reading a web address: https://www.example.org/news/today
PartExampleMeaning
Protocolhttps://How to connect. https is the secure way; http is not encrypted
Domainwww.example.orgWhich website
Path/news/todayWhich page inside the site

Browser features worth using

  • Tabs: keep several pages open in one window.
  • Bookmarks: save pages you will want again.
  • History: find a page you visited earlier.
  • Downloads: see what you saved and where it went.
  • Private window: nothing is kept on this device afterwards, but the sites you visit and your internet provider can still see where you went.
Worked example

Check you are on the real site

You want your school's website.

  1. Look at the domain, the part just before the first single slash, such as school.edu.
  2. Check for https and the padlock, which show a secure connection but not that the site is honest.
  3. Be wary of small differences such as scho0l.edu or school-edu.com.
  4. Better still, use a bookmark you saved yourself.

Answer. A padlock means the connection is private, not that the site is trustworthy.

Watch out

Pop-ups that say your device has a virus, or that you won a prize, are tricks. Close the tab and do not call numbers or install anything they offer.

Tip

Ctrl+T opens a new tab, Ctrl+W closes one, Ctrl+D bookmarks the page, Ctrl+L selects the address bar.

Check what you just learned

1. In https://www.example.org/news, which part is the domain?
  • https://
  • news
  • /news
  • www.example.org (correct)

The domain names the website.

2. What does a padlock in the address bar mean?
  • The connection is private (encrypted) (correct)
  • The site is honest
  • The page is free
  • The page is old

It protects the connection, not the intentions of the site.
keyPoints: A URL has a protocol, a domain and a path.
https and the padlock mean a private connection, not an honest site.
Use bookmarks for sites you rely on.

topics.title: Searching and judging what you find
topics.html:
A search engine looks for pages containing your words. The better your words, the better the answer. Then comes the harder part: deciding whether you can trust what you find.

Better searches
Instead ofTryWhy
photosynthesisphotosynthesis diagram class 8Adds what you need and who it is for
weatherweather in Pune tomorrowAdds the place and the day
how to fixhow to fix a phone that will not chargeSays what is wrong
python"python for beginners" free courseQuotes ask for the exact phrase

Search tools

  • Put an exact phrase in "quotation marks".
  • Put -word to leave a word out.
  • Use site:gov.in to search only inside one kind of site.
  • Use the Tools or Filters menu to limit by date.

Can you trust this page? Ask four questions

  1. Who wrote it, and are they an expert or an organisation you know?
  2. When was it written? Old pages can be wrong.
  3. Why was it written: to inform, to sell, or to persuade?
  4. Does another reliable source say the same?
Watch out

The first results are sometimes adverts, marked with a label such as Sponsored or Ad. They are paid for, not picked as the best answer.

Worked example

Check a surprising claim

A post says a famous exam has been cancelled.

  1. Do not share it yet.
  2. Search for the claim and look for the official board or a trusted news site.
  3. If only unknown pages say it, it is probably false.

Answer. Pause and check before you share.

Check what you just learned

1. What do quotation marks do in a search?
  • Nothing
  • Ask for that exact phrase (correct)
  • Make it faster
  • Hide adverts

They ask the engine to match the exact words.

2. Which question helps you judge a page?
  • What colour is it?
  • How long is it?
  • Who wrote it and why? (correct)
  • Is it popular?

Knowing the author and purpose tells you how far to trust it.

Key terms: flip and sort

Server
A computer that sends pages when asked
Browser
The app that opens web pages
URL
A web address
Protocol
How to connect: http or https
Domain
The name of a website
Search engine
A tool that finds pages containing your words
keyPoints: Specific words, quotes and filters give better results.
Ask who, when, why and whether others agree.
Adverts appear at the top of results; check the label.

modules.title: Email and online communication
modules.summary: Set up and use email, write messages that get answered, share files safely, and behave well online.
modules.outcome: You can send a clear, polite email with an attachment, manage your inbox, and communicate respectfully on any platform.
modules.intro: Email is still the main way schools, employers and offices contact you, and your email address is also the key to most of your online accounts. A clear message gets a quick reply. This module teaches the structure of a good email, the safe way to share files, and the manners that make online communication work.

topics.title: Anatomy of an email
topics.html:
An email has a few standard parts. Knowing what each is for prevents the two commonest mistakes: sending to the wrong people and being ignored.

The parts of an email
PartWhat it is forNote
ToThe people who must act or replyCheck the spelling of every address
CcPeople who should know, but need not replyEveryone sees who is in Cc
BccPeople copied privatelyOthers cannot see Bcc addresses: use it for large lists
SubjectA short, specific summaryThe subject decides whether it is opened
BodyYour messageShort paragraphs, one request
AttachmentA file sent with the messageCheck it is the right file and not too large
Worked example

A clear email

You want an extra day for a project.

  1. Subject: Request for one extra day for the science project.
  2. Greeting: Dear Mr Rao,
  3. Reason in one or two sentences, then exactly what you are asking for.
  4. Thank you, and your full name with your class.

Answer. Subject, greeting, reason, request, thanks and a sign-off: six pieces make a message people can answer in one line.

Habits of people whose emails get answered

  • One topic and one clear request per email.
  • A specific subject line, not Hello or Urgent.
  • Short paragraphs and plain words.
  • A polite greeting and closing.
  • Read it aloud once before you send it.
Watch out

Reply all sends your reply to everyone on the original message. Check who is in the list before you press it. Use plain Reply unless everyone really needs your answer.

Common mistakes

  • Writing in capital letters, which looks like shouting.
  • Sending an attachment you forgot to attach: mention the attachment in the body and check before sending.
  • Putting every recipient in To or Cc when addresses should be private: use Bcc.

Check what you just learned

1. Which field hides the other recipients' addresses?
  • To
  • Cc
  • Subject
  • Bcc (correct)

Bcc recipients are not shown to others.

2. Which subject line is best?
  • Request for one extra day for the science project (correct)
  • Urgent!!!
  • Hello
  • Question

A specific subject says what the email is about.
keyPoints: To is who must act, Cc is who should know, Bcc is hidden.
A specific subject and a clear request get answers.
Check recipients before Reply all.

topics.title: Attachments, links and your inbox
topics.html:
Sending a file is simple, but there are choices that make it safe and easy for the person receiving it.

Attach or link?
ChooseWhenWhy
Attach the fileIt is small (a few MB) and the person only needs to read itThey have it straight away
Share a link to a cloud fileIt is large, or several people will work on itOne shared copy; you control who can open it
Use a compressed (zip) fileYou are sending many files togetherThey arrive as one
Send a PDFYou want it to look the same everywhereA PDF cannot be edited by accident

Keep your inbox under control

  • Read, reply, file or delete each message; do not just let them pile up.
  • Use folders or labels such as School and Bills.
  • Star messages that need action.
  • Unsubscribe from newsletters you no longer read.
  • Check the spam folder now and then for real messages that landed there.
Watch out

Never open an attachment you did not expect, even from someone you know, without checking with them first: their account may have been taken over. Be most careful with files ending in .exe, .zip or .scr, and with documents that ask you to 'enable content'.

Worked example

Send a project safely

You must send a 12 MB report and a 25 MB video to a teacher.

  1. The report is small enough to attach, but turn it into a PDF first.
  2. The video is too large for most email; upload it to a cloud drive and send a link.
  3. Set the link so that only the teacher can open it.

Answer. Attach what is small, link what is large.

Tip

Mention an attachment in the body (I have attached my report as a PDF) and re-read before you press Send.

Check what you just learned

1. A 25 MB video is best sent by:
  • Attaching it
  • Uploading it and sending a link (correct)
  • Printing it
  • Splitting it into letters

Large files are shared as links.

2. A friend's account sends you an unexpected zip file. You should:
  • Open it quickly
  • Forward it to everyone
  • Check with your friend another way first (correct)
  • Delete the antivirus

Their account may have been taken over.
keyPoints: Attach small files; link large ones.
Use folders and unsubscribe to keep the inbox manageable.
Never open unexpected attachments.

topics.title: Online manners and messaging
topics.html:
Online messages lack the tone of voice and the face that make speaking friendly. A message that seems fine to you can read as cold or rude to someone else. A few habits help.

Say it better online
Instead ofTry
WHY DIDN'T YOU REPLYHi, I wanted to check whether you had seen my last message.
Fine.That works for me, thank you.
No.I am not able to do that, but I could do this instead.

Good habits in chats and groups

  • Reread before you send, especially when you are angry.
  • Never forward a message that was sent privately.
  • Ask permission before sharing someone's photo.
  • Do not reply to rude or unknown messages; block and report them.
  • Keep group chats on topic and avoid late-night messages to teachers.
Watch out

What you post can last. Messages and photos can be copied and shared by others even if you delete them. Pause before you post anything you would not want a future employer, teacher or relative to see.

Worked example

Respond to an unkind message

A classmate posts a rude comment about you in a group chat.

  1. Do not reply in anger.
  2. Take a screenshot.
  3. Tell a trusted adult and use the report or block options.
  4. If it continues, tell your teacher or a parent.

Answer. You do not have to put up with bullying, and keeping evidence helps people to act.

Definition

Digital footprint. The trail of everything you post, like, search and share online. Some of it is visible to others and some is kept by the services you use.

Check what you just learned

1. A message makes you angry. What should you do before replying?
  • Reply at once
  • Delete your account
  • Send it to everyone
  • Pause and reread, or wait until you are calmer (correct)

A calm reply is better than one you regret.

2. What is a digital footprint?
  • The trail of what you post and do online (correct)
  • A kind of virus
  • A file type
  • A website

It is the record your activity leaves.

Key terms: flip and sort

To, Cc, Bcc
Who must act, who should know, who is copied privately
Subject line
A short summary of the email
Attachment
A file sent with an email
Spam
Unwanted or junk messages
Reply all
Reply to everyone on the message
Digital footprint
The trail you leave online
keyPoints: Reread before sending; tone is easy to misread.
Block and report rude or unknown messages and tell a trusted adult.
What you post can last: think before you share.

modules.title: Safety and privacy
modules.summary: Build strong passwords, spot scams and malware, protect your privacy, and keep your files safe with updates and backups.
modules.outcome: You can protect your accounts and money from the commonest online attacks, and recover from a lost device or a mistake.
modules.intro: Almost every online problem people suffer comes from a small set of causes: weak or reused passwords, tricks that get people to hand over their details, and missing updates or backups. None needs technical skill to prevent. This module teaches the habits, and the reasons behind them, so they stick.

topics.title: Passwords and two-step verification
topics.html:
A password is the key to an account. Two things make a password strong: length and being unique to that one account.

Strong and weak passwords
PasswordWhy
riverlamp-planet-bicycle-orangeLong: four unrelated words are easy for you to remember and very hard to guess
Anaya2010Weak: a name and a birth year are easy to guess
Pass@123Weak: one of the first things attackers try
The same password on every siteRisky: one leak opens everything

What to do

  • Use a long passphrase of several unrelated words for important accounts.
  • Use a different password for every account; a password manager remembers them for you.
  • Turn on 2-step verification: after the password the account asks for a second proof, such as a code or a prompt on your phone.
  • Never share a password, an OTP or a PIN, even with someone who says they work for the bank or the company.
Worked example

Why two steps help

A scammer steals the password of your email.

  1. Without 2-step verification the scammer signs in at once.
  2. With it, they still need the code on your phone, which they do not have.
  3. They are stopped, and you receive an alert about the attempt.

Answer. Two-step verification protects you even when the password leaks.

Watch out

A bank, a government office or a company will never ask for your OTP, PIN or password by phone, text or email. If someone does, hang up; it is a scam.

Tip

Write your recovery options (a phone number and a second email) into your account settings now, while you can still sign in.

Check what you just learned

1. Which password is strongest?
  • Anaya2010
  • riverlamp-planet-bicycle-orange (correct)
  • password123
  • 12345678

A long passphrase of unrelated words is the strongest.

2. Who may ask you for your OTP?
  • Your bank on the phone
  • A delivery person
  • Nobody legitimate (correct)
  • A teacher

No legitimate organisation needs your OTP.
keyPoints: Length and uniqueness make a password strong.
Use a password manager and 2-step verification.
Never share an OTP, PIN or password with anyone.

topics.title: Scams, phishing and malware
topics.html:
Phishing means a message that pretends to be from a trusted source to get you to click a link, hand over details or pay. Malware is harmful software, often installed by a click on the wrong link or file. Both rely on tricking people, not on clever hacking.

Common scams and the tell-tale sign
ScamWhat happensThe sign
Fake bank call or textSomeone asks for your OTP, PIN or card numberA real bank never asks
Prize or lottery messageYou must pay a fee to claim a prizeA real prize does not charge you
Account will closeA link asks you to sign in right nowUrgency and a link
QR code to receive moneyYou are asked to scan or enter a PIN to receive moneyYou never need a PIN to receive money
Fake job offerYou must pay for training or a laptop firstA real employer does not charge to hire you
Virus warning pop-upA number to call or a program to installReal warnings do not tell you to call

Pause with the STOP rule

  • Stop: do not act on the first impulse.
  • Think: does this ask for money, a code or a login?
  • Observe: look at the sender and the link; something is usually slightly off.
  • Prove it: contact the organisation using a number or site you already trust.
Worked example

A text about your parcel

A text says your parcel could not be delivered and you must pay 25 rupees at a link.

  1. Stop: nothing is that urgent.
  2. Think: it asks for a payment through a link.
  3. Observe: you were not expecting a parcel, and the link is odd.
  4. Prove: ignore the text; check the courier's real app or site if you are expecting something.

Answer. Real couriers do not ask for card details through a random link.

Watch out

If you have clicked or paid by mistake, act fast: tell a trusted adult, change the password, call your bank on the number printed on your card, and report it. Do not feel embarrassed; many careful people are caught.

Check what you just learned

1. Someone asks you to enter a PIN to receive money. This is:
  • Normal
  • A bank offer
  • Required by banks
  • A scam sign (correct)

You never need a PIN to receive money.

2. What is the best response to an urgent message with a sign-in link?
  • Pause and check through a trusted route (correct)
  • Click quickly
  • Forward it
  • Reply with details

Urgency is the scammer's tool.
keyPoints: Scams trick people; they rarely need clever hacking.
Urgency, a link and a request for money or codes are the warning signs.
Pause, then check through a number or site you already trust.

topics.title: Privacy, updates and backups
topics.html:
Three more habits finish the job: control what you share, keep software current, and keep a second copy of what matters.

Habits and why they matter
HabitWhy
Check privacy settings on social media and appsDecide who sees your posts, photos and location
Share the minimumDo not post your address, phone number, school timetable or travel plans
Install updatesUpdates fix security holes that attackers use
Only install apps from the official storeOthers may carry malware
Back up what mattersA lost, stolen or broken device does not lose your work

App permissions: ask why

  • Does a torch app really need your contacts?
  • Does a game need your microphone?
  • Allow location only while using the app if it needs it at all.
  • Review permissions now and then and remove what you no longer use.
Worked example

Check one account

Do a ten-minute privacy check.

  1. Open the privacy settings of your most used app.
  2. Set posts to friends only and check who can see your photos.
  3. Turn off location sharing you do not need.
  4. Check which devices and apps are logged in and remove the ones you do not know.

Answer. A small regular check beats a big clean-up after a problem.

Watch out

A backup you have never tested may not work. Once, open a backed-up file on another device to check it.

Check what you just learned

1. What does the 3-2-1 rule say?
  • 3 passwords, 2 phones, 1 laptop
  • 3 copies, on 2 kinds of storage, 1 somewhere else (correct)
  • 3 apps, 2 folders, 1 file
  • 3 emails a day

It protects against any single loss.

2. Why install updates?
  • To change the colour
  • To use more storage
  • They fix security holes (correct)
  • To delete files

Attackers use known holes that updates close.

Key terms: flip and sort

Passphrase
A long password of several unrelated words
2-step verification
A second proof when signing in
Phishing
A fake message that tries to steal details
Malware
Harmful software
Backup
A second copy of your files
Permission
What an app is allowed to access
keyPoints: Share the minimum and check privacy settings.
Updates fix security holes.
Keep three copies, on two kinds of storage, with one somewhere else.

practical.title: Practical: a security check-up

modules.title: Everyday digital skills
modules.summary: Use online services, pay safely, fill in forms, fix common problems, and know where to find help.
modules.outcome: You can handle the online tasks of daily life, from booking and banking to troubleshooting, without fear and without taking risks.
modules.intro: Today, applying for a place, paying a fee, booking a ticket or finding a government service often happens online. The skills are the ones you already have: reading carefully, checking before you act and keeping your details safe. This module puts them together, and ends with a simple method for fixing common problems.

topics.title: Using online services safely
topics.html:
Online services (a school portal, a bank app, a government service, a shop) all ask for details and often for money. A short routine keeps you safe.

Paying safely online
DoDo not
Use the official app or type the address yourselfClick a payment link from an unexpected message
Check the amount and the name of who you are payingApprove a request you did not start
Use a payment method with a limit, or a virtual card, if availableSave card details on every site
Keep the receipt or confirmationPay an unknown person to claim a prize or a job
Worked example

Pay a school fee

The school sends a link to pay the fee.

  1. Check that the message comes from the school's usual number or email.
  2. Better still, open the school's website from a bookmark and find the payment page there.
  3. Check the amount and the school's name before you approve.
  4. Keep the receipt.

Answer. Going to the site yourself is safer than clicking a link.

Watch out

When you receive a payment request through UPI or another app that you did not start, decline it. You never have to approve a request in order to receive money.

Forms and personal details

  • Fill in only what is needed; ask why if a form wants more.
  • Use your real name where an official service requires it, and keep nicknames for social media.
  • Check what you typed before you submit.
  • Never send photos of cards, ID documents or OTPs in a chat.

Check what you just learned

1. You get a link to pay a fee. The safest route is:
  • Click it
  • Ignore the fee
  • Reply with your card number
  • Open the official site yourself and pay there (correct)

Going to the site yourself avoids fake links.

2. A payment request you did not start appears in your app. You should:
  • Decline it (correct)
  • Approve it
  • Ignore the phone
  • Call the sender back

You never approve a request to receive money.
keyPoints: Check the site, the connection and why a detail is needed.
Go to the official site yourself rather than clicking a link.
You never approve a request to receive money.

topics.title: Fixing common problems
topics.html:
Most problems are small and fixed by one of a few steps. Good troubleshooters follow a simple order and change one thing at a time.

Problem and first step
ProblemFirst step
A program is frozenClose and reopen it; if not, restart the device
A page will not loadCheck the connection with another site; restart the router
Storage is fullDelete what you do not need or move photos to the cloud
The device is slowClose apps, restart, check free storage and updates
A battery drains quicklyCheck which apps use it; lower screen brightness; update
You cannot sign inCheck caps lock and the address; use Forgot password
Worked example

The device that will not charge

A phone does not charge.

  1. Check the cable and the plug with another device.
  2. Clean the charging port gently.
  3. Restart the phone and try another charger.
  4. If it still fails, a repair may be needed; ask someone you trust.

Answer. Change one thing at a time, so you know what fixed it.

Watch out

Do not call a phone number from a pop-up or an advert for 'support'. Genuine help comes from the maker's official website or app, or a shop you know.

Tip

Take a screenshot of an error message, or write it down exactly. The wording is what lets a helper, or a search, find the cause.

Check what you just learned

1. What should you try first for a frozen program?
  • Buy a new device
  • Close and reopen it, or restart (correct)
  • Delete all files
  • Call a number from a pop-up

Restarting fixes most freezes.

2. Why change only one thing at a time?
  • It is faster
  • It saves power
  • You can tell what fixed the problem (correct)
  • It is the rule

Otherwise you cannot tell which step worked.
keyPoints: Restart first, change one thing at a time.
Write down the exact error message.
Use official support, never a number from a pop-up.

topics.title: Learning to keep learning
topics.html:
Technology changes. Nobody can learn every tool, but anybody can learn how to learn one when they need it.

A method for learning a new app

  1. Decide what you want to do, such as make a poster or track expenses.
  2. Look for a short beginner guide from the maker or a trusted site.
  3. Try it on something small and real, not just watching.
  4. Learn three shortcuts or features that save the most time.
  5. Keep notes of steps you will forget.
Where to get reliable help
SourceGood for
The app's Help menu or the maker's websiteOfficial, accurate steps
A teacher or a confident friendPersonal guidance
Short video tutorials from known channelsSeeing the steps
Library or community digital classesLearning with others
Worked example

Learn to make a simple poster

You need a poster for a school event.

  1. Choose a free design tool the school recommends.
  2. Open a beginner guide and follow the first steps.
  3. Make your poster with the event name, the date and a picture.
  4. Ask a friend to check it and note what you learned for next time.

Answer. Doing it for a real reason makes it stick.

Tip

Do not be afraid to click around. Most actions can be undone with Ctrl+Z, and nothing you do on a practice file can break the computer.

Check what you just learned

1. What is the best way to learn a new app?
  • Watch only
  • Avoid it
  • Memorise the menus
  • Use it on a small real task with a short guide (correct)

Doing is how learning sticks.

2. Where is a good first place to find help?
  • The app's Help menu or the maker's website (correct)
  • A pop-up
  • A stranger's message
  • An advert

Official help is accurate and safe.

Key terms: flip and sort

Official site
The real website of an organisation
Receipt
Proof of a payment
Troubleshooting
Finding and fixing a problem step by step
Screenshot
A picture of what is on the screen
Help menu
Built-in guidance in an app
Cloud storage
Files kept on other people's computers
keyPoints: Learn a new app by using it on a real task.
Use official guides and trusted sources.
Keep notes of what you learn.
